A Project Owner has full operational access to a project. This includes inviting and removing project members.

A Project User has mainly view-oriented access, such as viewing analytics, activities, and leads. Inviting or removing members is not allowed by default.

1. Open the project you want to add the team member to.
2. Go to Project Members.
3. Search for the person’s registered, verified user account.
4. Send the invitation and assign the appropriate project role.
5. The person receives an invitation by email and in the app.
6. They must accept the invitation. After acceptance, they become an active project member and the project appears in their project selector.

Le guide ne détaille pas les étapes exactes pour créer un projet. Il indique toutefois que la création passe par Project Onboarding et demande généralement :

1. Les informations de l’entreprise : nom, site web, logo facultatif, adresse et contact.
2. Les services ou produits et l’objectif principal de promotion.
3. Le profil du client idéal et les zones ciblées.
4. Les objectifs SEO.
5. Les noms ou URL des concurrents.

Pour connaître la procédure exacte dans votre interface, contactez le propriétaire du projet ou l’équipe Crawllex.

To invite a user to a project:

1. Open the relevant project.
2. Search for the user among registered, verified users.
3. Send the invitation by email.
4. The user accepts or declines the invitation in Crawllex.
5. Assign the appropriate project role.
6. After acceptance, the user appears as an active member in the project selector.

Only the project owner or an authorized member can send invitations.

لإضافة عضو جديد إلى المشروع:

1. اختر المشروع المطلوب.
2. افتح قسم أعضاء المشروع.
3. ابحث عن مستخدم مسجل وموثّق.
4. أرسل له دعوة عبر البريد الإلكتروني.
5. سيقبل المستخدم الدعوة أو يرفضها من البريد أو داخل Crawllex.
6. بعد قبول الدعوة، سيظهر العضو النشط في محدد المشاريع مع الدور المعيّن له.

General answer, not from your Crawllex data.

A canonical tag is an HTML tag that tells search engines which URL is the preferred, main version of a page when similar or duplicate pages exist.

Example:
<link rel="canonical" href="https://example.com/preferred-page">

General answer, not from your Crawllex data.

Organic click-through rate (CTR) is the percentage of people who click your unpaid search result after seeing it.

Formula: clicks ÷ impressions × 100

For example, 10 clicks from 200 impressions gives a 5% organic CTR.
